title: Distributional Shift Stress-Test for RLHF-Aligned Models

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Quantifying how alignment degrades under distributional shift directly informs deployment decisions: how much diversity is needed in alignment training data? The degradation curve would be a practical tool for practitioners.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Uses a publicly available RLHF-aligned model (no training required). Constructing a shift dataset by varying register/domain/framing is creative writing work accessible to beginners. Evaluation metrics (refusal rate, helpfulness) are straightforward. Medium compute for inference only.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: an alignment degradation curve across shift dimensions. However, varying three dimensions (register, domain, cultural framing) and measuring three metrics creates a large evaluation matrix. Could be tightened by focusing on one shift dimension.
